title: observability: propagate request-id + trace context, structured logs, per-endpoint metrics tags for API surface
author: Ava Chen
description:
Motivation: Improve observability for the API surface (hosted and OpenAI-compat endpoints) by propagating request IDs and trace context, emitting structured JSON logs with consistent fields, and tagging per-endpoint metrics so we can correlate latency/cost/quality regressions to specific routes and compatibility layers. This change targets streaming stability and function/tool-calling flows where tracing was previously lossy.

Summary:
- Propagate X-Request-ID (generated at edge) and W3C TraceContext (traceparent) through the gateway, router, runtime, and model worker boundaries.
- Attach request_id, trace_id, span_id, route, compatibility_layer and model_variant fields to all structured log entries emitted by api-gateway, router, runtime, and the OpenAI-compat adapter. Logs are emitted as single-line JSON to stdout/stderr for ingestion by our log collection pipeline.
- Add per-endpoint metric tags (route, method, compatibility_layer, model_variant, streaming boolean) to request latency, token_count, error_count, and stream_reconnect metrics.
- Ensure streaming responses (chunked + SSE) and tool/function-calling flows carry traceparent in the initial handshake and re-attach trace headers on reconnects so traces are continuous for long-lived streams.
- Updates to OpenAI compatibility layer: ensure compatibility adapter preserves request IDs and surface compatibility_layer tag in logs/metrics.

Implementation notes:
- Edge (api-gateway): generate X-Request-ID if missing; normalize W3C traceparent header; add to initial request context.
- Router: thread request_id + trace context into internal grpc/http2 metadata to model workers; add route metadata for per-endpoint tagging.
- Runtime/model-worker: attach request_id/trace to KV cache logs, batching logs, and token-emission events. For streaming, include request_id/trace in first chunk meta message (internal) and ensure reconnect flow replays header.
- OpenAI-compat adapter: map incoming openai-request-id to request_id if present; otherwise preserve X-Request-ID; add compatibility_layer=\"openai-compat\" tag to logs and metrics.
- Config: feature flag observable.api.enable_request_id_propagation (default on for prod), observable.api.log_format=json (default), observable.api.add_endpoint_tags=true.

Backward compatibility: Existing clients see no API surface change. X-Request-ID and traceparent headers are honored if provided. OpenAI compatibility responses now include an x-redwood-request-id header on success to aid correlating logs.

Testing: Unit tests for header normalization and header propagation added. Integration tests exercise streaming reconnect with traceparent and verify single-trace continuity. E2E staging run validated no regression for the /v1/chat/completions streaming path and function-calling flows.

Rollout plan: Canary deploy to region us-west-2 with 5% of traffic for 48h, monitor request_id uniqueness, trace sampling continuity, per-endpoint latency / error-counts, and log ingestion coverage. If stable, gradual rollout to remaining regions over 72h.

Related: ENG-1245 (observability backlog), ENG-1308 (streaming stability epic), SUP-987 (customer report about missing traces in tool-calls).
commit_summaries: edge: generate X-Request-ID when missing and normalize traceparent
gateway: attach request_id/trace to internal metadata and set x-redwood-request-id on responses
router: carry request_id + route into grpc metadata for workers
runtime: emit structured JSON logs with request_id/trace and add per-endpoint metric tags
openai-compat: preserve request ids and add compatibility_layer tag
tests: unit/integration tests for propagation and streaming reconnects
docs: added observability/requests.md and feature-flag notes
review_comments: Diego Morales: Please add a short note about what happens when traceparent is sampled out. Confirm we don't call StartSpan when trace is missing — just pass traceparent through., replied by Ava: We only forward the traceparent header; runtime uses traceparent to correlate logs but does not force-start spans unless sampling policy triggers. Unit tests added.

Priya Patel: Sizing question: does adding endpoint tags to every metric increase cardinality dangerously? replied by Ava: We limit tag sets to a fixed allowlist: route, method, compatibility_layer, model_variant, streaming; metrics are aggregated at the ingestion layer with a cardinality cap. Added config to toggle add_endpoint_tags.

Samir Gupta: Please verify streaming reconnect path for SSE and websocket transports. replied by Ava: Covered in integration tests; reconnect flow in streaming/reconnect.go re-injects request headers on re-attach and emits reconnect log lines with request_id/old_connection_id.
QA (R. Klein): Saw one intermittent failure in staging where x-redwood-request-id header was missing for 204 responses; fixed by ensuring middleware runs before short-circuit handlers.
release_notes: Improved API observability: request IDs and W3C trace context are now propagated end-to-end, structured JSON logs include request_id/trace and endpoint tags, OpenAI-compat adapter preserves request IDs and emits x-redwood-request-id. Operators can enable/disable per-endpoint metric tagging via feature flags.
